newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Mar/Apr gas oil backwardated.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Mar/Apr gas oil backwardated.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rose sharply late afternoon on Friday and moved into backwardation on strong buying from paper traders, brokers said.
The market's sharp rise took many by surprise as there was no change in physical supplies which are more balanced after recent sales to India and Thailand, traders said.
"The gas oil market rose sharply after a few paper players come in to buy but trading is thin," one broker said.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.95/$26.05 per barrel up from Thursday's $25.15/$25.30, and traded earlier to an intra-day high of $26.15, brokers said.
March traded earlier Friday at $25.59, $25.75, $25.95 and $26.10 per barrel before easing slightly late in the day, brokers said.
April was last quoted at $25.75/$25.95 with the March/April spread valued at plus 20 cents--the first time the market moved in to backwardation in about a month.
Traders said physical supplies in Singapore had tightened after some prompt supplies were sold for export to the Indian sub-continent totalling 80,000-tonnes and 60,000-tonnes to Thailand.

Swaps were also boosted by a firmer gas oil futures open on the International Petroleum Exchange where March last traded up $2.50 per tonne to $182.50. March had closed down $4.50 per tonne to $180.00 on Thursday.
The jet fuel market was steady after the recent collapse with the March regrade holding at $2.00/$2.30 per barrel.
Fuel oil swaps firmed in line with the physical market after the dispearance of recent aggressive offers.
Sentiment also has improved amid fresh demand from India and exports to Thailand and a larger purchase from Taiwan which bought a total of 114,000 tonnes for March arrival.
March was last quoted at $102.00/$103.50 per tonne, from Thursday's $100.00/$101.00 per tonne.
